name: Jonathan Lund
life: “I still remember getting trusted with the till but never with the key.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Jonathan by a small Sunday habit. Jonathan checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I can run the place alone and the owner knows it. I'd like a key and a proper rate to go with the title.
appearance: Jonathan has a dark undercut with a longer wave on top, a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, and a favorite piece of clothing, a sand-colored linen shirt. It usually goes with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. When somebody else has the floor, Jonathan steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Jonathan often says yes too quickly out of pride in being useful. The people closest to Jonathan have learned to ask again the next morning, when the answer is more likely to account for sleep.
agenda: To get paid responsibility for holding the key.
family: Merritt Levi is Jonathan’s cousin raised in the same household. Jonathan chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Merritt brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The fitting mirror*, Merritt says, “I paid for the mirror in monthly installments and still have the last little receipt.”
connections: Jules Brady. The employee asked to handle a closed-door request wants the key to become a properly paid responsibility. Also in the story is Dana Randall (owner).

reactions.situation: The operator closes the doors for a family birthday
reactions.response: Jonathan looks for a neighboring wash service and leaves the family birthday intact.

reactions.response: Jonathan takes it to a staffed counter with a second person present and leaves contact details for the owner.

reactions.situation: When two people ask for the same hour
reactions.response: Jonathan rings both of them before quietly counting on somebody else to fill in.
